o.norm: Fancy characters are not mapped by the default US mapping. https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CODEC-30

i.norm: U+00E9: LATIN SMALL LETTER E WITH ACUTE (é). Java classifies this as a letter, so the US-English Soundex mapping (which only covers A–Z) cannot handle it and must throw IllegalArgumentException.

Verifies that the default US-English Soundex mapping handles plain ASCII vowels correctly and rejects accented characters that fall outside the A–Z range.

Regression test for https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CODEC-30 — "fancy" (non-ASCII) characters must not be silently ignored or mis-encoded.
Plain lowercase 'e' is a vowel that anchors the Soundex code as the first letter.
é is recognised as a letter by the JVM but has no entry in the US mapping, so encoding it must throw IllegalArgumentException (not return garbage output).
If the JVM does not classify é as a letter, SoundexUtils.clean() strips it, leaving an empty string as the encoded result.
